sources.name: The Brass Plates
sources.desc: Israel's scriptures kept by Laban in Jerusalem — the five books of Moses, a record of the Jews down to Zedekiah, and prophets like Isaiah, Zenos, Zenock, and Neum. Brought to the promised land by Nephi; quoted throughout the record.

sources.name: The Small Plates of Nephi
sources.desc: Nephi's second, sacred record — 'the things of my soul' — passed from Jacob down to Amaleki, who delivered it full to King Benjamin. Mormon attached it whole because the Spirit whispered 'for a wise purpose.' It replaced the lost 116 pages.

sources.name: The Large Plates of Nephi
sources.desc: The national chronicle — reigns, wars, and ministries — kept continuously from Nephi to Ammaron, who hid all the records in the hill Shim and charged the ten-year-old Mormon to take them up.

sources.name: The 24 Gold Plates of Ether
sources.desc: The Jaredite record found by Limhi's 43 explorers among the bones of a destroyed nation, translated by King Mosiah with the interpreters.

sources.name: The Plates of Mormon
sources.desc: The gold plates delivered to Joseph Smith: Mormon's abridgment of the large plates, the small plates attached whole, Mormon's and Moroni's own words, Moroni's abridgment of Ether, and a sealed portion.

small-plates.name: Small Plates of Nephi
small-plates.desc: Unabridged personal ministry record, written by the prophets themselves.

mormon-abridgment.name: Mormon's Abridgment of the Large Plates
mormon-abridgment.desc: Mormon compresses ~500 years of the large plates, weaving in sermons, letters, and his own 'and thus we see' commentary.

mormon-own.name: Mormon's Own Record
mormon-own.desc: Mormon speaks directly — his editorial bridge (Words of Mormon) and his eyewitness account of the Nephite fall.

ether-abridgment.name: Moroni's Abridgment of Ether
ether-abridgment.desc: The Jaredite epic, retold by Moroni with his own sermons on faith and grace woven through.

moroni-own.name: Moroni's Own Record
moroni-own.desc: The last Nephite writes alone — ordinances, his father's sermon and letters, and the closing promise.
